text:
maria: Ran nsys profiles across the bisect range for the kernel-chooser tweak. Before->after shows a consistent 12-18% tail latency increase on 1k token traces. attaching quick notes below. :eyes:

ashok: ugh. can you paste the nsys timeline snippet or command you used?

maria: Sure — ran on the same machine, warm caches. Command:```nsys profile -o run_before --trace=cuda,osrt --capture-range=nvtx --sample=cpu python -m bench.run --model redwood-std --seq 1024 --runs 100``` and same with run_after after bisect. The timeline shows a cluster of memcpy activity aligned with the kernel switch.

devon: I pulled the timelines into a diff view. The big diff is this: before we had long-running matmul kernels (sm_optimized) with steady GPU occupancy. After the change the kernel chooser sometimes picks fallback_kernel_v2 which emits an extra cuMemcpyAsync per micro-batch to refill a temporary buffer. That memcpy shows up as these 400-700us slices between kernel launches.

sophie: any numbers on KV cache behavior? could the memcpy be caused by cache refills?

maria: KV hit rate jumped down: before - ~97% hits, after - ~88% hits on the same prompt set (measured via our perf hooks). Misses are small but they cluster and force a buffer materialization path.

ashok: can you paste the nsys callstack snippet for the memcpy hotspot?

devon: pasted excerpt (truncated):
```
Time(us)   Name                       Kernel/Callsite
---------  -------------------------  -------------------------------
1234567    cuLaunchKernel              sm_optimized_matmul
1235200    cuMemcpyAsync               device_buffer_refill (fallback_kernel_v2)
1236000    cuLaunchKernel              fallback_compute
1236800    cuMemcpyAsync               kv_prefetch_to_temp
```

devon: The second cuMemcpyAsync (kv_prefetch_to_temp) is new vs before. NVTX grouping shows it being triggered by the kernel-chooser policy which sets "materialize_temp=true" for sequences above N when fallback selected.

maria: bisect narrows to commit abc1f4d -> abc1f9a which is the kernel-chooser heuristics change (switch threshold and fallback enable).

perf-bot: Automated bisect: regression confirmed at abc1f9a (introduced by PR #8423).

ashok: so sounds like the chooser is too eager to use fallback, which in turn causes more KV cache refills that weren't necessary. We need to decide: tune chooser thresholds, change fallback path to avoid full memcpy, or make KV prefetch incremental.

sophie: can we repro with a smaller trace and add a scope to skip full materialize path? if yes we can micro-patch fallback to use in-place copies or reuse temp buffer.

maria: I did a quick micro-patch: change the fallback to reuse a per-thread staging buffer (avoid cuMemcpyAsync->device alloc pattern). Quick local run shows tail latency improves back to +4% (still a little overhead vs baseline, but much better than +15%). Patch diff:```diff --git a/runtime/chooser.cpp b/runtime/chooser.cpp
@@ -212,7 +212,10 @@ KernelChooser::select(...) {
-  if (should_materialize) { allocate_temp(); cudaMemcpyAsync(...); }
+  if (should_materialize) {
+    // reuse thread-local staging to avoid alloc+memcpy churn
+    temp = tls.get_or_alloc(staging_size);
+    cudaMemcpyAsync(temp, src, bytes, stream);
+  }
```

devon: nice. that's a low-risk micro-change. we should add a perf test to catch allocation+memcpy patterns at the kernel boundary.

ashok: Agreed. Action items: 1) land micro-patch behind feature flag (maria) 2) add perfreg test that asserts no unexpected cuMemcpyAsync in steady-state (devon) 3) revert or tune chooser default until we validate (sophie)

maria: I'll open a PR with the staging buffer patch + nsys flame diff in the description. I'll also attach the before/after nsys sessions and a small reproducer script.

perf-bot: NOTE: Uploaded nsys artifacts to /artifacts/2851234567/ (before.nsys, after.nsys, diff.html)

ashok: :thumbsup: thanks all. Let's be careful about defaulting the new chooser to avoid surprising customers.

maria: agreed. I'll add a rollout plan in the PR.
